# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

founder.order_why: It runs the way I'd pitch Fresco: name it, the market, who and when (supes in the trailer after the site walks), the daily-log problem, then the narrated-video scribe and how it fits Procore/ACC, and only then who gets asked.

founder.missing: Nothing about the money side. The flow never asked my price ($1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms), who pays (the general contractor, not the super), who at the GC decides, what the purchase involves (a trial on one live job, a Procore check, a security review), what it costs them today (the supers' hours on the log), or the commitment I'd ask for (a paid pilot on one site). Screen 19 offers a pilot without saying what it costs. Relative advantage also got a check screen but no 'what do you believe is true' screen, unlike Compatibility and Adoption friction.

PRIMARY.order_why: The noise question on screen 4 comes before screen 6 tells me I'd be talking over videos on my walks, so I was answering about talking on site before I knew that was the plan.
PRIMARY.missing: How long the log and photo uploads take me after the walks, whether Fresco puts the entry straight into the Procore or ACC daily log, whether the record would hold up in a delay dispute with the owner, and what it would cost.

screens.why5: The belief "Most would take short videos and talk over them on walks" is my first step word for word, with *their* habit kept and nothing added.
screens.why7: Both rows are steps the super takes themselves, each a base-form verb phrase of 9 words, neither another role's sign-off nor a Compatibility or Purchase point; the belief is my picked row, so a super's yes or no answers it, and the founder's escape is there.

screens.why1: Right after I said what they'd have to do to start, Keel playing back the efforts as rows to check is the obvious next step in the solution section.
screens.why2: Short videos, talking over them, walks and fixing the notes before they go out are how a super would say it, though 'on site walks' would read cleaner than 'on walks', and the intro repeats the title word for word.
screens.why3: Both are things a super does with his own phone on his own walk and in his own trailer, so he can answer from his day.
screens.why4: Two distinct efforts, the narrated capture and the review before it's texted or pushed to Procore, in plain field words, with nothing nonsense or overlapping and no third row needed.
screens.why5: It keeps my 'short videos with voiceover' as 'talk over them' and adds the review step that any super signing his own log would insist on, without naming Fresco or the contractor.
screens.why7: Both rows are base-form efforts the super takes himself, in one voice with no 'your', not Compatibility's Procore push or Purchase friction's sign-off, each one effort under 9 words, and the belief on the narrated video can go either way on Yes / Only if / Probably not / No.
screens.instead: Same rows, with the first read as 'Take short videos and talk over them on site walks'.

screens.why1: Right after I listed what supers have to do to start, it's obvious I now pick the one step most likely to stop them, and nothing earlier asked this.
screens.why2: Short videos, talking over them, site walks and fixing notes before they go out is exactly how I and my supers talk about the job.
screens.why3: I know which part my supers balk at, since I've watched them on walks, so I can pick from what I've seen rather than guess.
screens.why4: Both rows are distinct steps a super takes on their own, in my words; the narrated video, the one I picked, is the real catch, and nothing obvious is missing.
screens.why5: The picked row is my mechanism as I wrote it (short videos with voiceover on site walks), and the belief repeats it word for word with nothing reworded.
screens.why7: Each row is one effort the super takes themselves, in base-form verb phrases under nine words, and neither row is about Procore fit or getting it bought. The picked new habit can be supported by Yes / Only if or refuted by Probably not / No against the one-in-three bar, and the escape is owed on the stranger's item rather than here.

screens.why1: Just before the study goes out, it is obvious why Keel asks whether to collect emails from people who would try Fresco for real.
screens.why2: "Pilot" is plain to me, and the hint spells out the exact line respondents will see and where I will find the yeses.
screens.why3: Whether I want a list of supers or contractors to follow up with is my own call, and I know the answer.
screens.why4: Yes or no covers the choice cleanly, and no escape is needed for a founder's own decision.
screens.why5: To me a pilot is the paid pilot on one site that I typed as the Commitment step, but here it means a free email sign-up, and the screen doesn't say whether the superintendents, who don't pay, or the contractor ops leads get the line.
screens.instead: Ask people at the end to leave an email if they'd try Fresco on one of their jobs? (A sign-up list for follow-up, not your paid one-site pilot.) - Yes, ask them / No, don't ask

screens.why1: Picking who asks my supers the questions belongs right before launch, after the pilot offer and before people see the link, and nothing earlier asked it.
screens.why2: The question is plain, but the hint packs video, on-screen text, a preselect, a cost in credits and the text-message link into one paragraph, and it says Keel records 'the voice' while the interviewer appears on video, so I read it twice to know whether I'm choosing a face, a voice or both.
screens.why3: It's my own project and my own credits, and I know my supers are listening in a truck or a trailer, so I can judge which voice suits them.
screens.why4: Two named interviewers with a 5-second sample each are clear and distinct, but the screen is on video and offers only a voice to hear, with no look at the face, so I'm picking half of what my supers will see.
screens.why5: Nothing of my product, my price or my contractor buyer leaks into this screen, and it doesn't touch what I typed about Fresco.
screens.instead: Who should ask construction superintendents your questions? (Daphne is picked for you; she'll appear on video and every question is also written on screen. 400 credits either way.) — Daphne ▶ see and hear · 5 s / Saskia ▶ see and hear · 5 s

screens.why1: Right after choosing who asks the questions and just before sending, picking how my superintendents answer is the obvious next decision.
screens.why2: Plain words; "AI interviewer" and "read and tap" are clear to me as a founder who builds an AI scribe.
screens.why3: I know my supers are on phones in trailers or trucks at day's end, so I can judge whether they'd rather tap or talk to a video.
screens.why4: Three distinct, complete choices (video interviewer, text, let them pick) with no overlap, and no escape needed for a format choice.
screens.why5: It names my respondents as construction superintendents, keeps my study as typed, and leaks nothing of Fresco to them.

screens.why1: Right after choosing how superintendents answer, deciding who gets a link is the natural last step before sending.
screens.why2: Each option reads plainly on first pass; 'Contacts page' is Keel's own screen, which I've already been using.
screens.why3: I know whether I'm sending to supers I've met on Bay Area jobs, a searched list, or a group like a superintendents' forum, so this is mine to answer.
screens.why4: The three routes (named people, a Keel search list, one open link in a group) are distinct and cover how I'd actually reach supers, and my pick 'people I know by name' is there.
screens.why5: Nothing of my study is restated or changed here; it only asks how I'll reach construction superintendents.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' is plain, but the headline gives only '4 counted' and leaves the 5 needed to the cards below, so the deciding gap is not beside it.
screens.why_b2: The tally reads at a glance (3 of 3 too few, 7 answered) and the bar of 5 shows on each card, but it takes a second look to see why only 4 of my 7 counted, and the headline names only Compatibility.
screens.why_b3: Compatibility, Relative advantage and Adoption friction carry my three beliefs word for word, though the solution statement above them repeats itself ('gets back the notes with photos, assignees and due dates' twice).
screens.why_b4: Nothing tells me what to do: not whether to send the study to more superintendents, how many more I need, or whether to read the 4 answers I have.
screens.why_b5: No claim goes past the data; n=7 and 4 counted stay visible and every card says plainly it is too few to call.
screens.instead: Too few to call on all three: 4 of 7 counted, 5 needed; 3 were not counted because [reason]. Send the study to at least 1 or 2 more superintendents before reading anything into it.

screens.why_b1: "Too few to call" sits right beside "4 counted · 5 needed to call it", so I know where it stands and why at once.
screens.why_b2: The bars are clear and I can see 4 of 5 were counted, but the strip's "your bar · 4 of 5" with the marker at 4 reads like a count of people, not the 1-in-3 against line, so I had to look twice to see where my bar sits.
screens.why_b3: Compatibility and "Most construction superintendents could talk over the noise on site" are exactly the words I checked on the way in.
screens.why_b4: "Ray's no is the one to ask about" names someone to call, but the card never says to get one more counted answer, or what a No means for filming and narrating on the walk.
screens.why_b5: The low n is said plainly, but the question is pinned to my "last daily record", which I do in the trailer, not on the site walk where the noise is, and the quote under it is about a slipping schedule, not noise, so it hints at something these answers don't show.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of 4 could talk over the site noise, 1 couldn't (Ray), and you need one more counted answer; ask about the last site walk, not the daily record, and ask Ray what stopped him.

screens.why_b1: The status word *Too few to call* sits right beside the number that decides it, *4 counted · 5 needed to call it*, so I know why there's no verdict yet.
screens.why_b2: Better 3 (all a lot) against Same 1 out of 4 reads at once, but the strip's *your bar · 4 of 5* mixes the five-person floor with the one-in-three bar, and I had to look twice to see which the marker shows.
screens.why_b3: The name and the belief line are mine word for word, but the *You said hours back at the end of the day.* line drops my second benefit, action items to the crew the same day, so the card misquotes half of what I checked.
screens.why_b4: *Nothing is settled here yet* is generic and doesn't tell me the plain next step: get one more superintendent's answer (or a firmer one from Luis) to call it.
screens.why_b5: The n stays visible, Luis's guess is set apart, and the screen calls 3 of 4 *a lean, not a call* rather than a result, so nothing claims more than four people can carry.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of 4 said a lot better, 1 said no difference, so it leans your way, but one more counted answer is needed to call it. Send it to one more superintendent. You said hours back at the end of the day and action items to the crew the same day.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know why there is no verdict yet and which number decides it.
screens.why_b2: The bars and the for/against cells are plain, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' with the marker at 4 needs a second look to square with 'no more than 1 in 3 say probably not or no', '4 counted' and '5 needed' all on one screen.
screens.why_b3: The card is Adoption friction and the belief 'Most would take short videos and talk over them on walks' is the line I checked on the way in, word for word.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic; it doesn't tell me to get at least one more superintendent counted, or that two of my three yeses hang on not slowing the site walk, which is the thing I'd have to prove in the product.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible (5 answered, 4 counted, Luis set aside as a guess), the small group is called 'a lean, not a call', and nothing claims the belief held.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of 4 counted would do it, but 2 of those only if it doesn't slow the walk. Get one more super counted, and show that narrating doesn't add time on the walk.

screens.why_b1: Each box opens on "Too few to call" with "4 counted · 5 needed to call it" right under it, so I know nothing is decided and exactly why.
screens.why_b3: Compatibility and Relative advantage carry the names I checked, and the belief lines are word for word the ones I approved, the noise on site and the hours back with action items the same day.
screens.why_b4: "5 needed to call it" tells me one more counted answer would settle each line, but the screen never says to send the study to more supers, and it doesn't explain why Adoption friction has no box.
screens.why_b5: n is on every box, the low count is named as too few to call, and each group of one shows as "(1)" with a single quote, so nothing reaches past the four who answered.
screens.why_b6: Ray's "the log can wait till morning, the deck can't" and Denise's "done on the tablet before I leave the gate" both say the schedule and no-show subs eat the day, not the log, which I hadn't typed and which questions where my hours-back benefit lands.
screens.instead: Too few to call on both: one more superintendent's answer would decide each, so send the study to more supers; nobody was against Adoption friction, so it has no why here; and both who disagreed say the schedule and subs eat the day, not the log.

screens.why1: Opening on which platform my jobs run on is the obvious first gate for a study about getting site photos and notes into the daily log.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are the names every super at a GC uses daily, and 'jobs you run' is how I'd say it myself.
screens.why3: I know exactly what platform each of my jobs is on, with no guessing.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it cleanly for a screener with no escape, and 'any of the jobs' handles a super running more than one job.
screens.why5: It keeps the founder's segment, Procore or ACC, without leaking anything about the product or its plan.
screens.why6: One short question with a yes-or-no; 'ACC' is said as letters on site all the time, so it hears fine.

screens.why1: Right after checking my jobs run on Procore or ACC, asking whether I got caught with the daily log this week is the obvious next thing.
screens.why2: Leaving site with the daily log not done is how I'd say it myself, and I can answer it on one read.
screens.why3: I know exactly whether I walked off the job this week with the log still open, so it's my own week I'm answering from.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it cleanly, and the chips belong to the story box after a Yes, not to this question.
screens.why5: Nothing of the product leaks, but the problem has drifted from typing the log up after the walks to leaving site before it's finished, so a super who sits in the trailer an hour typing it up before heading home has the problem and still says No.
screens.why6: One short question in plain words, then 'Yes or no', easy to hear once and answer.
screens.why7: It's a true two-way gate in the window and not the circumstance everyone's in, but it has moved off the founder's counted problem (typing up the log after the walks) to a narrower result, so the share undercounts the people the belief is about.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you type up the daily log after your site walks? Yes · No

screens.why1: I've just answered about Procore and leaving site before my daily log was done, so being shown an idea about getting site walk notes into Procore is an obvious next step.
screens.why2: Site walk, crew, action items, assignees and Procore or ACC are all my words, but nobody on a job calls anything a 'scribe', and 'narrated site walk videos' takes a second read.
screens.why3: I do site walks every day, shoot photos and video on my phone, hand out punch items to subs and push things into Procore, so I can picture this on my own job.
screens.why4: A card to read, no options.
screens.why5: It's an idea card shown on purpose, and nothing of anyone's internal terms for me slipped into the earlier questions; the belief about use during the walk reads straight.
screens.why6: Heard once, the opening 'AI scribe that turns narrated site walk videos into notes' is a mouthful, though the rest is short sentences I can follow and 'A-C-C' is how we say it anyway.
screens.instead: Imagine Fresco, an AI tool for site walks. You take short videos on your walk and talk over them. It turns them into notes with photos, who's on it and when it's due, texts the crew their items, and sends it all to Procore or ACC in one click. The people building it believe you'd use it during the site walk.

screens.why1: Right after the Fresco card it makes sense to ask whether I could even narrate out loud on my site, since that is what the thing depends on.
screens.why2: I call it my daily log, not a daily record, and 'talked over the noise' doesn't say talked into what, my phone or to my foreman, so I'd read it twice.
screens.why3: The noise is on the walk, not when I'm writing the log at the trailer, so pinning it to my last daily record makes me guess which part of the day they mean.
screens.why4: Easily, most of the time, sometimes, no covers it for a loud site, and I can't tell fits if I never tried.
screens.why5: Nothing of their product leaks past the card, but the idea's step of speaking into the phone got dropped to just talking, so it drifted a little.
screens.why6: Short, one question, four short options I can hold and one escape at the end.
screens.why7: An ability with the four ability rungs in order, two for and two against, so it can hold or fail, with I can't tell set apart as the escape.
screens.instead: On your last site walk, could you have spoken into your phone over the noise? Yes, easily / Yes, most of the time / Only sometimes / No, or I can't tell

screens.why1: Right after the idea card and the noise question, asking whether Fresco would have beaten how I did my last log is the obvious next thing to ask.
screens.why2: I'd answer it, but 'keep an accurate record of the day's work on site' isn't how I talk; it's my daily log, and the screen before already called it my daily record.
screens.why3: I do a log every working day, so I know exactly how the last one went and can judge whether narrating a walk would have beaten it.
screens.why4: The four answers run cleanly from a lot better to worse, they don't overlap, and 'I can't tell' fits as the escape.
screens.why5: Nothing of the product leaks past the card shown on purpose, but the founder's own job phrase is pasted in word for word, so it reads like their wording rather than my log.
screens.why6: Heard once it's two short sentences and four short options I can hold, with the escape said last.
screens.why7: The four fixed answers, their order and the lone 'I can't tell' escape all match the card, but the occasion is any last log rather than the hard one where the job was at stake (the day I left before the log was done), and the stem skips 'Fresco, what it is'.
screens.instead: Think of the last day you left site before your daily log was finished. Would Fresco, an AI scribe that turns narrated site walk videos into notes, have done that log better for you, or not? A lot better · A little better · No difference · Worse · I can't tell

screens.why1: Right after asking whether Fresco would keep my daily record better, it's obvious to ask whether I'd actually change how I walk the site to use it.
screens.why2: Short videos, talking over them and site walks are how I already talk about my day, so I'd answer this on first read.
screens.why3: I walk the job every day with my phone out taking photos, so I know whether I'd film and talk instead.
screens.why4: The four answers run cleanly from yes to no, and the catch on my site walk is the real one, since a walk that drags is what would stop me; I can't tell fits as the out.
screens.why5: The card says plainly what it is, and the step is said in my words, with nothing of the founder's plan or roles leaking through.
screens.why6: One short question with four short answers I can hold, then the one out, all easy to hear once.
screens.why7: The effort is mine to take, a new habit on every walk; the options run two for and two against with a specific condition, and the I can't tell escape is there and apart.
